_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

run.note: Release checklist for 1.49.3, the first release since the 1.49.1 run. Product changes since 1.49.1: the 1.49.2 checklist fixes (pack guard for the bundled weights, bundled-model warning wording, widened FusionLeader for full recall), bm25 hash tie-break (#702), ADR-0107 PC.0-PC.4 exit-message follow-up (#700), and the WebGPU intra-op spinning change (#712). The 1.49.1 run's three dropped items (attach-or-start-identity-proof, f49-secret-layout, busy-bank-refusal-and-best-effort-bump) are restored here; see findings-against-prior-runs. The global tool was force-installed from the local Release pack (uninstall+install: dotnet tool update refuses to replace an already-installed same version). The reinstall replaced the 1.49.3 store directory the owner's running :7721 server loaded from; that server stayed alive and kept answering 401.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The run note says: 'Not re-run this time: attach-or-start-identity-proof, f49-secret-layout, busy-bank-refusal-and-best-effort-bump (no changes to their code paths since 1.44.0 by commit subjects; not re-verified).'
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: Those three items are absent from the 1.49.1 items array entirely, not marked skipped with a reason. The JSON therefore shows an 18-item checklist with no trace of the three dropped checks, while all three features still exist in the product (ADR-0106 identity proof and secret layout, and the bank-busy refusal path).
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: python3 parse of 2026-09-24-1.49.1-release.json: 18 items, none named attach-or-start-identity-proof, f49-secret-layout or busy-bank-refusal-and-best-effort-bump. All three were run this time and passed (see the items below).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Coverage silently shrank by three items and a reader of the checklist cannot see it. Per the skill, an item is deleted only when its feature no longer exists; these should have been kept or skipped with a reason.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: write-path-noise-filtering: 'each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to' — status pass.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The 1.49.1 item never read the registered policy set; its own evidence admits 'The registered-policy set was not re-read from source this run'. It could not have failed if a second registered policy were broken, because it never knew how many policies were registered.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: AppRegistrations.cs:332 is the only INoiseFilterPolicy registration at v1.49.3 (HermesProcessNoisePolicy); the 1.49.1 evidence names rejections from that one policy only.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The item as written was unfalsifiable on policy count. This run reads the registration in source first, then probes every shape the registered policy declares.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The run is presented as a finished result ('17 pass / 1 fail', commit 656eaaed).
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: full-recall-ranking-order carried accepted=null, which the skill defines as unanswered — a run with any null left in it is unfinished, not a run with no objections.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: 2026-09-24-1.49.1-release.json, items[full-recall-ranking-order].accepted == null (every other item was true).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The unanswered item was resolved by the 1.49.2 FusionLeader fix and passes this run, but the 1.49.1 checklist shipped without an acceptance decision on its one failure.
